200.description: Local only: the config file the daemon loads and watches, the SHA-256 of the content it last handled, pending restart-only keys and the file's current error

get.description: Local only. Paired devices (token hashes are never returned).

put.description: Remote listener and relay tunnel only. Requires a paired device bearer token with either view or decide scope.

delete.description: Remote listener and relay tunnel only. Requires a paired device bearer token with either view or decide scope.
Local only. Revokes a device immediately: later requests get 401 and its open event WebSockets close.

patch.description: Local only. Update enabled, push, or scope (view or decide); at least one field is required. Muting push preserves API/event access. Scope changes apply immediately. Disabled devices get 403 and their event WebSockets close with code 4403.

400.description: Invalid or empty body; submit scope cannot be changed

101.description: WebSocket events: {type, request} for request.created (carrying the final status, so auto-handled requests arrive already decided), request.decided, request.expired and request.cancelled; request.updated when a pending request's desktop run starts, a stop is requested, or its claim is released or interrupted (`request.run`); {type: yolo.changed, yolo} when YOLO mode changes or its timer ends; {type: keys.changed, keys} when the shortcut overrides change; {type: config.changed, config: ConfigChange} after every config save (file edit, `handup config set`, or a Settings save): `applied` keys are in force, `restart_required` keys wait for a daemon restart, and `error` (`path:line: message`) means the file is invalid and the previous config stays in force. Refetch `/v1/ui-settings` on it. Closed immediately when the calling device is revoked (4401) or disabled (4403). The daemon sends a WebSocket ping every 25 s, so a client that hears nothing for longer can treat the connection as dead

get.description: Resolved requests, newest resolution first, with cursor pagination. history.keep_days/max_requests and best-effort history.max_bytes bound retained requests; history.files_keep_days can expire files while keeping history.

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: approved, denied, expired, cancelled, auto (rule or YOLO decision), or dismissed (info notice)

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only requests with a preview of this type

parameters.name: has
parameters.description: attachments: any file, files, image, pdf, audio, or video preview

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Request kind: command, edit, review, question, info, or custom

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive search in title, summary, and cwd

put.description: Replace the keyboard shortcut overrides (`keys:` in the daemon config): validated, saved to the config file and applied without a restart. Emits `keys.changed` so every open client rebinds, then `config.changed`. Local, and decide scope on paired devices.

200.description: The saved overrides, keys in canonical form

400.description: Unknown action, built-in key, unparseable key, conflict, invalid config file, or the daemon has no config file

get.description: Trial and license state. `locked` means new requests are refused with HTTP 402 (`code: license_required`); pending requests stay decidable. Development builds report `not_enforced`.

put.description: Activate a license: `key` is exchanged at gethandup.dev for a signed license (online); `license` installs signed license text (offline import). The license is verified with the embedded public key and stored (0600) in the data directory.

400.description: Key rejected, invalid license, or not exactly one of key and license

delete.description: Remove the local license files. The trial start stays recorded.

post.description: Local only. Atomically fetch and mark delivered unread non-empty replies to info notices. Supply session, id, or both (both selectors must match). An id alone claims a notice without a session. First consumer wins; no selectors is invalid.

Local only (unix socket or loopback bearer). Issues a one-time pairing code for `handup pair`. With `relay: true`, opens a fresh relay channel and returns a relay pairing link that carries the channel, the device's relay credential, the daemon's Noise public key, and the code.

409.description: Remote access (or the relay) is off or has no reachable base URL

502.description: The relay refused or could not be reached

post.description: Remote listener only. Trades a one-time pairing code for a device token. Rate-limited per peer IP; every attempt counts.

402.description: License required: the trial ended or the license was revoked (`code: license_required`; see `GET /v1/license`)

post.description: Send a fixed synthetic approval or question to try the inbox. Missing body or kind defaults to approval; no client-supplied request content is accepted.

403.description: Remote device without decide scope or submit token

get.description: Audit events of one request, oldest first (created, decided, expired, cancelled), with the deciding device's name when it is still paired.

200.description: Claimed: `run` is set (with `run.timeout_ms`, the request's `run_timeout` or `run.timeout`, capped at `run.max_timeout`) and no other decision, expiry, or timeout applies until the desktop app reports the result, the request is cancelled, or the lease (limit plus 2 minutes) lapses
Run claim dropped (the command never started)

post.description: Stop a desktop run from any client: local callers, and paired devices with decide scope. Audited as `run_stop_requested`.

200.description: Stop requested: `run.stop` names who asked and `request.updated` is emitted; the desktop app running the command stops it (TERM, then KILL after 5 s) and reports `stopped from <device>; terminated|killed`. Repeating it changes nothing

403.description: Remote device without decide scope, or disabled, downgraded or revoked by the time the stop commits

409.description: Not pending, or no desktop run holds the request

200.description: Ordered rules (`rules:` in the daemon config) followed by session rules
Rule removed: a session rule, or one from `rules:` in the daemon config (rewritten and applied live; emits `config.changed`)

get.description: Disk usage by category (request history, audit log, files, free database pages, other), request counts, the history retention policy and the running or most recent cleanup. Local, and view scope on paired devices.

post.description: Start a background cleanup of resolved requests (never pending ones or files they reference). It runs in small batches, so requests and decisions keep working. Local, and decide scope on paired devices.

409.description: A cleanup is already running; `job` is that cleanup

get.description: Progress of a cleanup. Local, and view scope on paired devices.

404.description: Not the running or most recent cleanup

post.description: Cancel a cleanup. Local, and decide scope on paired devices.

200.description: Stops after the current batch; what was already removed stays removed

404.description: Not the running or most recent cleanup

get.description: What a cleanup would remove now, for the inline confirmation. Local, and view scope on paired devices.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: history (requests, audit, unshared files) or files (files only)

parameters.name: older_than_days
parameters.description: Only requests resolved at least this many days ago; 0 or absent = every resolved request

parameters.name: keep_newest
parameters.description: Keep the newest this many resolved requests; 0 or absent = no count limit

put.description: Set history.keep_days and/or history.files_keep_days: saved to the daemon's config file and applied without a restart. A shorter period starts a cleanup at once. Local, and decide scope on paired devices.

400.description: Out of range, or the daemon has no config file

200.description: Local only: metadata, never secrets or hashes

201.description: Local only: new submit secret (shown once) and integration metadata

400.description: Invalid name, expiry, or duplicate name

200.description: UI policy: undo window, primary action side, HTML network access, remote mode/warning, relay pairing, calling device, pending config restart and config error. Refetch on `config.changed`.

get.summary: Build of the running daemon, so clients and `handup doctor` can spot a daemon left over from an older install.

200.description: Local only: daemon version and commit

get.description: YOLO mode: off, on (auto-approve new low and medium risk requests) or hard (every risk). Runtime only; a daemon restart turns it off.

put.description: Set YOLO mode, optionally `for` a duration after which it turns off. Applies to requests created afterwards; matching rules still win and requests that need a human answer (questions, fields, feedback policies, several approve options) stay pending. Emits `yolo.changed`.

Answer.description: The human's answer to one question.

selected.description: Chosen option labels; at most one unless the question is `multi`.

text.description: Typed answer; only when the question allows free text.

device_name.description: Name of the paired device when `actor` is `device:<id>` and that device is still paired.

device_kind.description:
What that paired device is: `app` (the handup phone app) or `browser`
(a paired web browser). Absent for other actors, revoked devices, and
devices paired before the daemon recorded it.

CleanupEstimate.description: What a cleanup would remove right now (an estimate: requests keep resolving).

requests.description: Resolved requests deleted (0 for a files-only cleanup).

bytes.description: Approximate bytes freed: file sizes plus, for history, request and audit rows.

CleanupJob.description:
A background cleanup. The daemon runs one at a time in small batches, so
requests and decisions keep working while it runs.

keep_newest.description: Newest resolved requests kept; 0 = no count limit.

total.description: Items to process, counted at the start: requests (history) or files (files).

bytes_freed.description: Bytes freed: removed files plus database pages released by deleted rows.

compacting.description: Returning freed database pages to the filesystem (incremental vacuum).

CleanupScope.description:
Which resolved requests a cleanup covers (`POST /v1/storage/cleanup` body,
`GET /v1/storage/estimate` query). Both limits apply together.

older_than_days.description: Only requests resolved at least this many days ago; 0 = every resolved request.

keep_newest.description:
Keep the newest this many resolved requests (requests resolved in the
same millisecond as the last one kept stay too); 0 = no count limit.

ConfigChange.description: `config.changed` payload: what a config save did.

applied.description: Dotted keys whose new value is in force now (`keys.approve`, `rules`, `notifications.enabled`).

restart_required.description:
Dotted keys whose saved value differs from the one the daemon started
with and that apply only at the next daemon start (listen addresses,
remote access and relay, upload limit). Cumulative: empty again once
the file matches the running daemon.

error.description:
`path:line: message` when the file failed to parse or validate; the
daemon kept the previous config.

ConfigStatus.description:
`GET /v1/config/status` (local only): the daemon's config file and the
content it last handled.

path.description: The config file the daemon loads and watches; null without one.

sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the file text the daemon last read or wrote.

restart_required.description: Restart-only keys saved since the daemon started.

error.description: The file's error (`path:line: message`) while the previous config stays in force.

oneOf.description:
The desktop app ran the request's command for the human: this is how
it ended. Present only on approved command requests decided by Run.

DecisionFields.description:
Decision `fields`. Question requests carry only `answers`, keyed by question
id; other requests carry answers to `input.fields` or edited tool input.

Device.description:
A paired remote device. The bearer token itself is never stored; only its
SHA-256 digest is (see `remote::hash_token`).

scope.description: `view` (read-only) or `decide` (adds decision, cancel and test requests).

Email.description:
An email draft for review. handup never sends it: on approval the agent
sends the draft (or the edited `decision.fields`) with its own mail tool.

date.description: Date shown in the header, as the agent formats it (e.g. RFC 2822).

body.description: Message body as Markdown (plain text renders as-is).

body_html.description: Optional HTML alternative; rendered only in the sandboxed HTML preview frame.

oneOf.description: The message this draft replies to, shown collapsed under the body.

blob.description: Uploaded blob hash (`POST /v1/blobs`) so the reviewer can open the file.

body.description: Plain text of the earlier message (or a snippet of it).

History.description:
Retention for resolved requests (decision history). The daemon prunes at
start and hourly; 0 disables a cap. Pending requests are never pruned.

keep_days.description: Delete resolved requests older than this many days (0 = no age cap).

max_requests.description: Keep at most this many resolved requests (0 = no count cap).

max_bytes.description: Best-effort live database/WAL/blob byte cap, excluding free database pages (0 = unlimited).

files_keep_days.description: Remove files belonging only to resolutions older than N days (0 = request lifetime).

resolved_at.description: Unix milliseconds when the request left `pending`.

IntegrationToken.description: Named submission credential. Secrets and digests are never serialized.

keys.description: Action id → key; an omitted action uses its default, so `{}` resets all.

LicenseSet.description:
`PUT /v1/license` body: exactly one of `key` (exchanged online at
gethandup.dev) or `license` (signed license text, for offline machines).

locked.description: True when new requests are refused (`expired` or `revoked`).

enforced.description: False in development builds; release builds always enforce.

trial_days_left.description: Whole days left in the trial (rounded up); null once licensed.

trial_ends_at.description: Unix ms when the trial ends (ended).

display_key.description: Masked key, `****-XXXXXX`, from the installed license.

checked_at.description: Unix ms of the last successful online check with Polar.

revoked_reason.description: Why the license is revoked (`revoked`, `disabled`, `not found`, ...).

message.description: How to fix a locked daemon; null otherwise.

NoticeReply.description: A human's optional reply to an info notice, delivered to the first consumer.

code.description: One-time code (single use, expires after 2 minutes).

url.description: Pairing page URL; the code travels in the fragment so it never reaches server logs.

fingerprint.description: TLS leaf certificate SHA-256 fingerprint when the remote listener uses TLS.

PairCreate.description: Local-only: create a pairing request (body for `POST /v1/pair`).

name.description: Device name; the pairing page may suggest one when empty.

relay.description:
Pair through the end-to-end encrypted relay (`remote.relay.url`)
instead of the remote listener.

cookie.description: Browser flow: set `HttpOnly` session cookies instead of returning the token.

token.description: Long-lived device token (`hu_` + 64 hex). Omitted in the cookie flow.

host.description:
This computer's name (its hostname), so a device paired with several
computers can tell them apart. Absent when unknown.

Question.description: A question for the human; answered in `decision.fields.answers[id]`.

id.description: Stable id, unique within the request.

allow_free_text.description: Allow a typed answer besides (or instead of) the options.

label.description: Answer text; unique within its question and returned in `selected`.

description.description: One-line explanation shown under the label.

preview.description: Markdown shown while the option is focused (code blocks allowed).

callback_url.description: Terminal-event destination; requires the daemon callbacks.allowlist.

timeout.description: Optional positive duration, at most one year. Absent uses config; null/`none` disables expiry.

run_timeout.description:
Optional limit for the desktop app's Run of this command (e.g. `30m`).
Absent uses the daemon's `run.timeout`; the daemon caps it at
`run.max_timeout`. Not part of the request's decision timeout.
Must be between 1ms and one year.

oneOf.description: Present while the desktop app runs the command (daemon-managed).

run_interrupted.description:
Unix milliseconds when a desktop run's lease lapsed without a result
(the app crashed or stopped responding); the request is decidable
again. Cleared when it is run again (daemon-managed).

RequestInput.description:
Request `input`. Only `kind: question` requests interpret `questions`;
other keys (for example raw agent tool input) pass through unchanged.

fields.description: Generic form fields (`text`, `textarea`, `select`, `boolean`) for non-question requests.

questions.description: Structured questions (1..=10) for `kind: question`; answers arrive in `decision.fields.answers`.

oneOf.description:
The cleanup that applies a shorter period now; null when nothing
shrank or another cleanup is running (hourly retention then applies it).

RetentionUpdate.description:
`PUT /v1/storage/retention`: the "keep for" control. Omitted fields keep
their value; 0 keeps forever (files: as long as their request).

RunClaim.description:
The handup desktop app on this computer is running the request's command
right now. While the claim holds, the request stays pending but no other
decision, expiry, or timeout applies; cancelling it stops the run. Set and
cleared only by the daemon.

started_at.description: Unix milliseconds when the run was claimed.

lease_until.description:
Unix milliseconds after which an unreported run no longer holds the
request (the app crashed or lost the daemon): the run limit plus
[`RunClaim::GRACE_MS`].

timeout_ms.description:
The run limit in milliseconds: the request's `run_timeout`, else the
daemon's `run.timeout`, capped at `run.max_timeout`. The desktop app
stops the command when it is reached.

oneOf.description:
Someone asked to stop the run from another client (phone, browser,
CLI, another desktop); the desktop app running it stops it.

RunResult.description:
Outcome of running a command request in the handup desktop app. The
command already ran: an agent must not run it again. Output is the
redacted tail of each stream.

exit_code.description: Process exit status; absent when it never started or a signal ended it.

stdout_tail.description: Last bytes of standard output (at most 64 KiB), credentials redacted.

stderr_tail.description: Last bytes of standard error (at most 64 KiB), credentials redacted.

duration_ms.description: Wall time from start to exit, in milliseconds.

truncated.description: Earlier output was dropped from either tail.

elevated.description: Ran with administrator rights (pkexec on Linux, osascript on macOS).

error.description:
Why it did not finish normally: timeout, cancellation, signal, or a
start failure (for example pkexec missing or authentication refused).

content_hash.description: Content hash the window showed; the claim fails if the request changed.

RunStop.description: A stop request for a running command (`POST /v1/requests/{id}/run/stop`).

by.description: Who asked: the paired device's name, or `this computer`.

integration.description: Server-verified integration token name; caller values are overwritten.

session_title.description: Display-only session name; scoped rules always use the session ID.

StorageReport.description:
`GET /v1/storage`: usage by category, the retention policy, and the
running or most recent cleanup.

StorageUsage.description: Disk space the daemon uses, by category. Categories add up to `total_bytes`.

total_bytes.description: Database file, write-ahead log, and stored files on disk.

history_bytes.description: Request rows (with their inline previews) and their indexes.

files_bytes.description: Stored files (preview blobs) plus their metadata rows.

free_bytes.description: Free database pages; new requests reuse them before the file grows.

other_bytes.description: Everything else: devices, tokens, schema, and the write-ahead log.

oldest_resolved_at.description: Unix milliseconds of the oldest resolution still kept.

compacts.description:
The database returns freed pages to the filesystem after a history
cleanup (`auto_vacuum=incremental`, set on databases created by this
version). Otherwise freed pages stay in the file as `free_bytes` and
are reused.

UiSettings.description: Read-only UI policy derived from daemon config; never includes secrets.

primary_side.description:
`decisions.primary_side`: right or left, the edge of decision footers
that holds the primary (approve) action. Apps may override it per device.

keys.description:
`keys:` keyboard shortcut overrides (action id → key, e.g. `shift+a`,
`mod+enter`); absent actions use their defaults. Changes arrive live
as `keys.changed` events.

remote_warning.description: Direct-mode risk warning; UIs show it as a persistent banner when set.

pair_relay.description:
`remote.relay.url` is set, so local callers can pair through the relay
(`POST /v1/pair {relay: true}`). Always false for paired devices.

oneOf.description: The calling paired device on the remote listener; null for local callers.

config_restart_required.description:
Config keys saved since the daemon started that apply only after a
restart (`config.changed` `restart_required`); empty when none.

config_error.description:
The config file's parse/validation error (`path:line: message`) while
the daemon keeps the previous config; null when the file is valid.

for.description: Optional duration (`15m`, `1h`); absent = until turned off. Not valid with `off`.

until.description: Unix milliseconds when the mode turns itself off; null = until turned off.
